newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady as SBI, RBI buy dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady as SBI, RBI buy dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.8175/8225 against the dollar on Wednesday, little changed from 35.8150/8250, dealers said.
"There were no surprises today," the chief dealer at a leading bank said.
The rupee eased to the 35.83 level early in the day as dollar demand from the State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest commercial bank emerged.
Dealers had expected SBI demand on Wednesday ahead of a strike in the bank's regional offices on Thursday which threatens to disrupt forex operations at its Calcutta office.
"But SBI's volume (of demand) was not much and he started bidding down," said a dealer.
This led to the rupee touching a high of 35.81.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) then stepped in to buy dollars, aimed at maintaining the exchange rate rather than pushing down the rupee, dealers said.
The forward dollar premiums edged down, tracking a fall in overnight call money rates and continued exporter sales.
The six-month annualised forward dollar premium closed the day at 4.13 percent compared with the previous close of 4.30 percent, dealers said.
"I guess forward premium has touched a bottom," said a dealer.
